verdictBasis: REJECT: 1 blocker, 1 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. All six folded findings — CLAUDE-V8-B1, CLAUDE-V8-S1 and Codex SARIFV8-S1 through S4 — are repaired at their named targets, the successor roster is clean for the first time since v7, and all five obligations pass. The blocker is that v9 declares a new pinChainRule requiring every pin record to enumerate the full roster of the file it pins, and then breaches that rule on both pins it adds.

priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the Claude 2 reviews of v2 (ACCEPT — wrong), v3, v5, v7 and v8. v9 folds my CLAUDE-V8-B1 and CLAUDE-V8-S1, and CLAUDE-V9-B1 again concerns how the ledger records one of my own verdicts alongside Codex's. Both findings are stated as single-command re-derivable facts: advisory rosters inside two files v9 pins by digest, and a byte-comparison of one string against its v8 predecessor. I also record a miss of my own: Codex's SARIFV8-S3 and S4 are both real and I did not find either at v8. I checked the input arm's enum for law/schema divergence and did not run the same check against expectedWhenNotProduced and expectedWhenProduced, where the same defect shape was present. That is why the structured expected schemas are re-checked directly here rather than accepted from the repair notes.

blockers.title: v9 declares a pin-enumeration rule and breaches it on both pins it adds, erasing six advisories
detail: v9 strengthens pinChainRule to read: 'Each successor pins the verdicts it folds. Every pin record enumerates the full blocker, shouldFix, and advisory roster of the file it pins. Earlier pins recover via basedOn.sha256.' The middle sentence is new at v9 and is the class-level rule both reviewers asked for at v8. It is normative and unqualified.

Instance 1, and the reason this is blocker-grade. appliesFindingsOf.codexv8 records advisories: []. The file it pins reproduces at f7061826ecc7592ea609f736a46818c5d0297da695a9a610a55efa7a64423e56 and carries advisoryCount 3 with advisories SARIFV8-A1, SARIFV8-A2 and SARIFV8-A3. An empty array is not an omission; it is an assertion that the pinned file has no advisories, and that assertion is false.

Instance 2. appliesFindingsOf.claude2v8 carries no advisories member at all. The file it pins reproduces at bfa3a001faf7188c0332bf3322f0db4c7e591069852ecedebae19e59ea385094, mode 0444, and carries advisoryCount 3 with ADV-SPC-V8-01, ADV-SPC-V8-02 and ADV-SPC-V8-03. Under the old practice this was an incomplete record; under v9's own new rule it is a breach of a stated requirement.

Both older pins are correct — claude2v5 lists its four ADV-SPC-V5-* and claude2v7 lists its four ADV-SPC-V7-*, each matched by a notFoldedThisSuccessor line. So v9 repaired the two historical instances and reproduced the defect on both records it newly created, in the same object, in the same commit that declares the rule forbidding it.

Six advisories leave the ledger as a result, and notFoldedThisSuccessor names none of them. At least one is a live technical item rather than bookkeeping: SARIFV8-A1 records that hostLocationList constrains each entry's role token but never requires exactly one primary, forbids multiple primaries, or defines the no-primary case. I confirmed that gap persists in v9 — hostLocationList's members are entry, name, orderLaw and standing, with no cardinality rule.
blockers.whyBlockerGrade: This is the fourth consecutive generation in which the fold ledger loses the advisories of a digest-pinned verdict: v7 asserted a false empty array, v8 omitted the member, and v9 now does both at once. What makes it a blocker rather than a repeat SHOULD-FIX is that v9 supplies its own standard to be judged against. A successor that writes an unqualified enumeration rule into its ledger and then violates it twice in the adjacent records has not repaired the class it claims to have closed; it has documented the class and left it open. The false empty array on codexv8 is independently blocker-grade on the standard I applied at CLAUDE-V7-B1 and would be so with or without pinChainRule.
blockers.gradingNote: I have kept the two instances in one finding because they are one rule, one object and one fix. If the coordinator prefers them separated, instance 2 is at minimum a SHOULD-FIX on its own; neither reading permits ACCEPT.
blockers.minimumRepair: Set codexv8.advisories to [SARIFV8-A1, SARIFV8-A2, SARIFV8-A3] and add claude2v8.advisories as [ADV-SPC-V8-01, ADV-SPC-V8-02, ADV-SPC-V8-03], then add notFoldedThisSuccessor lines for both sets in the form already used for the v5 and v7 rosters. Carry SARIFV8-A1 forward explicitly as an open technical item on hostLocationList rather than letting it lapse with the ledger entry.

The identifier spaces actually in play at this generation are CLAUDE-V8-B1/S1, ADV-SPC-V8-01..03, SARIFV8-S1..S4 and SARIFV8-A1..A3. The note names none of them.
/appliesFindingsOf is on the closed roster and other members of it were updated, so this is not a silent path — the note was simply left behind while the object around it moved.

This is not a cosmetic field in this chain. CLAUDE-V5-S1 was caused by exactly the confusion idCollisionNote exists to prevent: a Claude v3 REJECT recorded under Codex's SARIFV3-* namespace. Folding a generation whose two reviewers used CLAUDE-V8-* and SARIFV8-* without stating that separation removes the guard at the point it is needed.

The successor roster is clean again. What remains is one object. A v10 needs: codexv8.advisories = [SARIFV8-A1, SARIFV8-A2, SARIFV8-A3]; claude2v8.advisories = [ADV-SPC-V8-01, ADV-SPC-V8-02, ADV-SPC-V8-03]; notFoldedThisSuccessor lines for both; and idCollisionNote updated to the v8 namespaces. Worth noting for the coordinator's judgement: v9 wrote the correct general rule into pinChainRule and then did not apply it to its own new records, so the fix a v10 needs is compliance with a rule already on the page, not a new rule. Carrying SARIFV8-A1 forward as an open technical item on hostLocationList would also stop the one erased advisory that is not bookkeeping from lapsing.

summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX, both in the fold ledger and neither in the projection law. All six folded findings are repaired at their named targets and I verified each against bytes: basedOn.method's three deleted clauses are restored and the v8-to-v9 leaf diff puts zero of 39 changed paths outside the roster, the first clean successor diff since v7; claude2v7 now carries its four ADV-SPC-V7-* identifiers with a matching not-folded line; expectedWhenNotProduced.reason is narrowed to the single reachable value; and expectedWhenProduced now structurally requires runId on the run and findingId and coverage per result while correctly leaving verdict conditional. All five obligations pass and OBL-3 is discharged for the first time. The blocker is that v9 adds to pinChainRule the sentence 'Every pin record enumerates the full blocker, shouldFix, and advisory roster of the file it pins' — the class-level rule both reviewers asked for — and then breaches it on both records it creates: codexv8 asserts advisories:[] where the pinned file carries SARIFV8-A1, A2 and A3, and claude2v8 omits the member where the pinned file carries ADV-SPC-V8-01, 02 and 03. Six advisories leave the ledger, among them SARIFV8-A1's live hostLocationList primary-cardinality gap, which I confirmed is still unrepaired in v9. Separately, idCollisionNote is byte-identical to v8's and names only the v7 and v5 namespaces while v9 folds the v8 generation, removing the collision guard at the generation where CLAUDE-V8-* and SARIFV8-* are in play.
verdictStatement: This independent review rejects sarif-projection-contract.v9 at the measured subject digest and HEAD 2d5f15b, which was stable at both ends. It does not apply or seal the candidate, change the DR-122 register standing, advertise preview SARIF, resurrect G17, mint Run/Finding/D9 recipes or a D-096 (A) grant, or authorize docs/v2/implementation/.
